newsitem.title: HONG KONG: OECD sees HK spreading business rules to China.
newsitem.headline: OECD sees HK spreading business rules to China.

text.p: Hong Kong's reversion to China could help spread application of the rule of law in business to the giant nation, to the benefit of both China and the world, the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development said.

"Hong Kong's international reputation as an economy strongly committed to the application of the rules of law in business practice may make it an important catalyst for the diffusion of these rules to the rest of China," the OECD said.
"If so, the process of China's integration with the rest of the world will be significantly eased and gains for China and the rest of the world increased," it said.
The capitalist British colony reverts to Chinese sovereignty at midnight on June 30 next year, but will maintain autonomy on economic affairs and remain a separate customs territory.
"The combination of Hong Kong and China will form one of the most dynamic economic regions in the world," the OECD said in a special section of its semi-annual economic outlook.

Since economic links between the two have long been increasing due to Hong Kong's role as an intermediary between China and the rest of the world, the short-run economic effects of the handover are likely to be fairly minor, the OECD said.

Hong Kong is China's second-largest trading partner, Hong Kong-owned industries employ about four million workers in China's southern province of Guangdong, and Hong Kong accounted for about 60 percent of China's stock of foreign investment.

In the longer term, Hong Kong is expected to play a continuing and crucial economic role for the rest of China as a major trading partner and provider of services, although some other cities such as Shanghai may come to rival its role, the OECD said.
